core_struggle: I'm anxious about how things will turn out
mirror: You put in the mehnat, and the fikar about the result is what makes the work go bad.

queries.hook: The frustration of working hard and watching the result worry steal the quality from the effort itself.
queries.diagnose: When the mind grips the outcome, honest effort turns into anxiety; the more you hold on to the result, the worse the work becomes.
queries.steady: Your effort is yours and the result is not; do the work and let the result go, and the work will find its own quality.
queries.act: Do your work fully and let the result go; practise doing the work for the work itself and not for what it will bring.
queries.story: A warrior who fought with everything he had, and was told to fight without attachment to the fruit, shows you what the Gita means.

bridge: What you are living with is what the texts call holding on to how it turns out, and that is where this week begins.
week_thesis: Seven days from watching the result steal your work to letting the effort itself be the reward.

week_beats.hook: You recognise the frustration of good work spoiled by worry.
week_beats.diagnose: You see that the fikar is the root cause, not the work itself.
week_beats.steady: You hold that your effort is yours and the result is not.
week_beats.story: A warrior who fought without attachment to the fruit shows you what the Gita means.

insight: You do the work, but the mind is running after a result it cannot hold. That is what spoils the effort.
details: is asking what the Gita teaches about this
